It's great that counseling has helped with your self-esteem and self-blame—that's real progress worth acknowledging. For cutting down on alcohol, some approaches that can help include identifying your triggers and planning ahead for high-risk situations, setting clear limits before you drink, removing alcohol from your home, and finding alternative activities or coping strategies for stress. Connecting with support groups like SMART Recovery or AA can also provide structure and community.

That said, since you're looking to make significant changes to your drinking patterns, it's worth discussing this with a healthcare provider or your current counselor. They can help you explore whether medical support might be appropriate, especially since reducing alcohol use can sometimes involve withdrawal risks depending on your patterns. They can also help you build a personalized plan that fits your life. You don't have to figure this out alone, and reaching out for that kind of support is a strength, not a weakness.
